name: EMBECTA

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: -5% is too generous; the market's -8 to -10% is the right number or still kind. The decline is accelerating, not a one-off step: revenue fell 3.8% in FY25 and about 9.5% organically in FY26. Inside FY26, Q3 net-price erosion from payer mix was worse than Q2, and retail insulin-pen prescriptions fell a little faster. Both weekly basal insulins were approved within six months of each other. The guide implies Q4 adjusted operating margin near 17%. Owen Mumford and international are lower-margin than the US business they replace. My $165M base already credits cost savings that have not yet appeared in a full quarter. A highly levered equity facing a 2028 covenant step-down and a 2029-30 refinancing wall deserves a cost of equity well above the engine's 10%, which pushes WACC toward 9.5% and fair value toward $3.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Q4 FY26 results and the first FY27 guide (expected late Nov 2026). The specific tells: US revenue below about $110M a quarter, FY27 adjusted operating margin guided below 22%, net leverage not falling despite $150M+ of paydown, and any weekly-insulin uptake commentary.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Partly. The Q3 price hit ($20.1M), management's statement that the payer-mix impact on net price was greater than in Q2, the slightly faster prescription decline, the Onswik approval on 2026-09-24, and the guide-implied Q4 margin are all on the record.
devils_advocate.unresolved: I could not get FY27 guidance (none exists yet), market prices or yields for the 2030 notes, quarterly US insulin-pen prescription data, the lead-plaintiff outcome, or any Section 232 consumables decision. I also cannot separate how much of Q3's $25M sequential US recovery was one-time restocking. The counter is not decisively proven, but I cannot refute it with evidence either, so I do not call the stock cheap.

what_changed:
Since the FY2025 10-K (Nov 2025):
(1) 2026-05-05, Q2: US share loss at one large retailer to a low-cost needle, falling insulin-pen prescriptions, adjusted EPS guide cut about 40%, quarterly dividend cut from $0.15 to $0.01, and a 3-year buyback of up to $100M. The stock fell 57.8%. 2.68M shares were repurchased at $3.23-3.29 in May-June.
(2) 2026-05-15: Owen Mumford acquisition closed (GBP 100M plus up to GBP 50M earn-out; $128.4M cash net of cash acquired; funded by a $180M revolver draw). It added two UK plants, one Malaysian plant and a US warehouse, and contributed $13.8M of Q3 revenue in about 1.5 months.
(3) 2026-06-17: securities class action Apitz-Grossman v. Embecta, D.N.J. 2:26-cv-07217 (class period 2025-11-25 to 2026-05-04). The company calls it without merit. I found no lead-plaintiff order after the 2026-08-17 deadline.
(4) 2026-08-06, credit agreement First Amendment: revolver cut to $310M; $210M extended to 2028-12-30 at SOFR+350; $100M still due 2027-03-31; tighter covenants (first-lien net leverage max 4.75x through 2027-06-30, stepping to 3.75x from 2028-04-01; interest cover min 2.5x, rising to 3.0x from 2028-01-01); monthly liquidity reporting to the revolving lenders.
(5) 2026-08-07, Q3 FY26: revenue $271.7M (-8.1%); US $120.8M (-24.6%); international $150.9M (+11.5%); adjusted operating margin 25.5% vs 36.9%; FCF $40.7M; $53M of debt repaid. FY26 guide: revenue $1,015-1,035M reaffirmed; adjusted operating margin raised to 23.5-24.0%; adjusted EPS $1.80-1.90; FCF about $100M including $18-20M of capex; interest about $95M; tax 27%; at least $150M of debt repayment ($128M done through nine months). Share was stable in Q3. There is no FY27 guide, and the long-range plan update is not due until late calendar 2027. A new North America president joined from Sandoz generics.
(6) 2026-09-24: FDA approved Lilly's once-weekly efsitora (Onswik), the second weekly basal insulin after Awiqli (2026-03-26).
(7) The Section 232 investigation into medical consumables, open since Sep 2025, still had no proclamation as of early October 2026 per trade trackers. Chinese syringes already carry 100% Section 301 duties.
(8) Price: $6.45, against a 52-week low of about $2.89, up 99% over 63 days.
consensus_case: At $6.45 the market prices Embecta's free cash flow to the firm to shrink about 6-9% a year for five years (my $165M base, WACC 8.35-9.35%, the engine's 2% terminal), and the evidence for a shrinking core is strong. FY2026 adjusted organic constant-currency revenue is guided down 8.8-10.2%; US revenue fell 20.6% in the first nine months and 24.6% in Q3 after a large US retailer moved to a lower-cost pen needle. Q3 alone lost $20.1M to price and $19.9M to volume year on year. Management said the customer and payer-mix hit to net price was larger in Q3 than in Q2, and the year-on-year decline in retail insulin-pen prescriptions was slightly faster. Gross-to-net deductions rose to $157.2M on roughly $429M of Q3 gross sales (36.7%, vs 32.6% a year earlier). Adjusted gross margin fell from 67.2% to 58.2%. Two once-weekly basal insulins are now FDA-approved: Novo's Awiqli on 2026-03-26, with US launch in 2H 2026, and Lilly's Onswik (efsitora) on 2026-09-24. Each cuts a basal patient from 365 needles a year to 52. Oral GLP-1s (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) and automated insulin delivery for Type 2 keep delaying or replacing injections. The guide implies Q4 adjusted operating margin of about 16-18%, against 25.5% in Q3, which was flattered by distributor orders normalizing after a Q2 destock. On the balance sheet: $1,469M of principal debt, 3.7x net leverage, and covenants that step down to 3.75x first-lien net leverage and 3.0x interest cover in 2028. The revolver was cut from $500M to $310M, with $100M still maturing 2027-03-31, and the lenders now require monthly liquidity forecasts. The $639M term loan (Mar-2029) and $700M of notes (Feb-2030) have to be refinanced off a smaller EBITDA. Equity is about 20% of enterprise value, so one turn of EBITDA multiple moves the stock by roughly $5-6 a share. The stock has already doubled from about $3.2 since the Q3 beat, so the stabilization re-rating has happened.
base_case_rationale:
Base case: FCFF falls 5% a year from a normalized base of about $165M. That base is unlevered, treats stock compensation as a cost, and is my own construction, not the engine's.

Building the base from the FY26 guide: FCF of about $100M plus after-tax interest ($95M x 0.75 = $71M) gives $171M. Expensing stock compensation (about $21M) leaves $150M. Adding back about $26M of after-tax stand-up, brand-transition and Owen Mumford deal costs gives about $176M. Two adjustments bring that to about $165M: Q1 FY26 earned above the post-shock run rate (adjusted operating income of $79M, against a Q2-Q4 average of about $55M), which takes off about $18M; a full year of Owen Mumford plus the cost-review savings adds back about $5-7M.

Why -5% a year: US pen needles keep falling at roughly 6-8% a year, driven by the two weekly insulins, oral GLP-1s, automated insulin delivery for Type 2, and net-price resets to low-cost competitors. International, about 55% of revenue, grows low single digits in constant currency, helped by Latin America and Asia, held back by China. Owen Mumford (about $92M of annual revenue per the user's Q&A pack) grows high single digits. GLP-1 co-packaging and US small packs are real but small. The cost review offsets part of the negative operating leverage, and capex normalizes near $20M.

Where this differs from the screen: the naive baseline (3-year revenue CAGR of -1.5%) predates the FY26 step-down of about 9.5% organically. The engine's $81M FCFF base omits about $80M of after-tax interest (see data quality) and averages in the FY24 TSA-exit year.

Fair value in my base case: $12.33 with the engine's 2% terminal at its own corrected WACC of 8.35%. It falls to $6.16 with a 0% terminal, and to $7.85 or $3.26 at a 9.35% WACC with 2% or 0% terminal (subtract about $1.47 a share for claims the extract leaves out: $30.9M of finance leases, $14.2M of issuance costs netted against debt, and the $38.1M Owen Mumford earn-out liability). That range brackets $6.45. Once corrected, the whole gap rests on two choices the cash flows cannot settle: whether a pen-needle franchise whose drug partners are actively removing injections deserves a 2% perpetual growth rate, and a 3-point-a-year difference in FCFF decline that FY27 guidance has not yet tested. That is not an edge.

I am not supplying final_growth, as with ALKS on 2026-08-31. The reprice reads the committed extract, which has no interest expense for this name. Its WACC therefore comes out at 5.5% (a 'no/low debt' 5.8% cost of debt on a B-rated, 80%-debt capital structure), and -5% would be recorded as a $38.99 fair value (+505%). fcff_base_override cannot repair a discount rate.
key_risks: Core US pen-needle volume and net price keep falling: weekly basal insulins (Awiqli 2026-03-26, Onswik 2026-09-24), oral GLP-1s, AID pumps for Type 2, low-cost needles at large retailers

Leverage: $1,469M principal at 3.7x net; covenant steps to 3.75x first-lien net leverage from 2028-04-01; $100M revolver tranche due 2027-03-31; $639M term loan Mar-2029 and $700M notes Feb-2030 to refinance off a smaller EBITDA
Gross-to-net creep: deductions 36.7% of Q3 gross vs 32.6% a year earlier; variable-consideration liability $159.4M vs $113.7M at FY25 year end
BD dependency: BD supplies all cannulas, holds the IP, and may terminate the supply agreement on a change of control, which limits a sale as an exit
Securities class action (D.N.J. 2:26-cv-07217) at an early stage
Section 232 medical-consumables remedy still pending; buy-local pressure abroad

Net leverage vs the 4.75x covenant now and the 3.75x step-down from 2028-04-01; any refinancing or extension of the 2029 term loan
